churn_resistance.rationale: The core is well-contained (one data-access module, full boundary types, single config source), but per-page RxJS pipelines, triplicated speciesById logic, four copies of the title rule, and a non-strict hand-written tsconfig mean both requirement changes and the inevitable resource-API migration will ripple across many files.

findings.issue: Data loading is built entirely on the RxJS generation (switchMap/combineLatest/forkJoin/shareReplay + toSignal) repeated in every page, while Angular 22 (current stable) promotes resource/rxResource/httpResource to stable and the official skill guidance prefers httpResource for reads.
findings.suggestion: Model each page's data as httpResource/resource derivations in the shared data layer (e.g. one resource per route param), keeping the multi-request fan-out in a single service so future framework guidance lands in one place.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled tsconfig omits "strict": true (and strictTemplates is not enabled), so the compilerOptions and template type-checking are weaker than the CLI-generated defaults a fresh v22 project gets.
findings.suggestion: Add "strict": true and "strictTemplates": true to match CLI defaults; the codebase's explicit null handling suggests it would mostly pass unchanged.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is declared as a runtime dependency but never imported anywhere in the app.
findings.suggestion: Remove @angular/forms from dependencies (native controls with (input)/(change) handlers are used).

findings.issue: The speciesById lookup Map is rebuilt identically in move-page.ts:41-49, type-page.ts:39-46 and ability-page.ts:31-38.
findings.suggestion: Expose speciesById once from CatalogService (it already builds such maps in catalog.service.ts:81) and inject it in the three pages.

findings.issue: The document-title rule '<h1> – Pokédex' is re-implemented with an effect in four page components (pokemon-page, move-page, ability-page, type-page) plus two constructor calls.
findings.suggestion: Use the router's Route.title with a custom TitleStrategy so the naming rule lives in app.routes.ts / one provider.

findings.issue: Runtime configuration is read from a window.__POKEDEX_API_BASE_URL__ global injected by server.mjs:11-14, requiring a declare-global contract shared between server and app code.
findings.suggestion: Consider the documented runtime-config pattern: a small config document consumed via provideAppInitializer, keeping the contract typed in one module.

findings.issue: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush is set explicitly on every component, but OnPush is the default in Angular 22, so this is copy-pasted boilerplate a newer release would not generate.
findings.suggestion: Drop the redundant changeDetection properties (harmless, but it's noise the framework no longer scaffolds).

findings.issue: The '#moves' anchor jump is implemented with an effect reading window.location.hash plus setTimeout + getElementById().scrollIntoView, bypassing router navigation primitives.
findings.suggestion: Once withExperimentalPlatformNavigation / router scroll handling is stable, move this to the router; at minimum centralize the hash handling in one place.

findings.issue: parseQuery casts the ActivatedRoute query map with 'as unknown as Map<string, string>' to work around the ParamsMap type.
findings.suggestion: Use the ParamsMap interface's methods directly (params.get) instead of casting; it removes a type hole at the URL boundary.

summary: This is a modern, well-structured Angular 22 codebase: signals everywhere, new control-flow syntax, standalone components, functional providers, zoneless by default, and all HTTP access funnelled through two typed services. The main forward-looking gap is that the data layer is entirely the RxJS Observable generation (switchMap/forkJoin/toSignal) at the exact moment Angular 22 promotes httpResource/resource to stable as the recommended read primitive, so a migration will eventually touch every page. Secondary risks are an unused @angular/forms dependency, a hand-written tsconfig that silently disables strict/template type-checking, and small duplications (speciesById, title effects) that will ripple on requirement changes.

httpResource for reads per angular.dev guide and Angular v22 release notes

redundant: OnPush is the default in Angular v22
